specification.problem: Prepare the ground state of a diagonal EC3 (exact cover, 3-bit) problem Hamiltonian H_P on n=3 data qubits by a digitized adiabatic evolution from H_B=-sum X_i, with optional ancilla-controlled phase-kick filter steps, then read the solution by computational-basis measurement of the data qubits.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=3 variables, a few EC3 clauses (each clause penalizes all bit triples except those with exactly one 1), unique satisfying assignment; M about 10-50 first-order Trotter slices; noiseless statevector simulation. Outside scope: the paper's fast random or regular signal sequences, the randomized Trotter formula, decoherence or system-bath effects, and the trapped-ion implementation. The phase-kick filter is a sketch-level proposal, not the paper's method.

symbols.meaning: diagonal problem Hamiltonian; zero energy exactly on satisfying assignments
spectral gap of H(s) between ground and first excited state

equations.label: Interpolating Hamiltonian
equations.description: Standard AQC interpolation between driver and problem Hamiltonian.
equations.justification: The abstract describes AQC generically with a final Hamiltonian encoding the solution; the linear interpolation and H_B are standard choices.

equations.label: EC3 problem Hamiltonian
equations.description: Each clause c on three variables adds a penalty projector onto the 5 forbidden triples (all except exactly-one-1). It is diagonal and expands into Z, ZZ terms. For a clause, the penalty is (1/2)(1-(1-z_a... ) ) form; equivalently the clause cost is (s-1)^2 with s=sum of the three bits, giving Z and ZZ terms only.
equations.justification: The abstract names EC3 but not its Hamiltonian; this is the usual EC3 definition, and the concrete clauses must be chosen for the instance.
assumptions: Penalty per violated clause is 1 (or the squared-sum form (x_a+x_b+x_c-1)^2)
Clause set chosen to have a unique solution

equations.label: First-order Trotter slice
equations.description: Digitized adiabatic evolution; exact only as dt goes to 0 and approximate otherwise. The H_P factor is exactly a product of commuting Z-rotations (RZ, CX-RZ-CX); the H_B factor is a product of RX(-2(1-s_k)dt).
equations.justification: The abstract proposes a randomized Trotter formula, but the details are absent; the ordinary first-order formula is used as a stand-in.

equations.label: Local adiabatic schedule
equations.description: Local adiabatic rule giving a slow sweep near the minimum gap; g(s) is computed classically by exact diagonalization for this tiny instance, and s_k is obtained by discretizing the integral.
equations.justification: Roland-Cerf local adiabatic rule, recalled from background; the sketch requests it.
assumptions: g(s) known classically for the 8-dimensional instance
c sets the total time T

equations.label: Ancilla phase-kick filter (sketch)
equations.description: Controlled short evolution from an ancilla in |+>/|0>, followed by the inverse kick to return the ancilla to |0>. With ancilla returned to |0> and the data unchanged, the net data effect is the identity unless the kicks differ; as written it is not a verified filter.
equations.justification: Proposed in the sketch as a stand-in for the paper's fast signals; applying a kick and its exact inverse is the identity, so a nontrivial filter needs a different construction, which is unspecified.

equations.label: Readout and success probability
equations.description: The final state is measured on the data qubits and the most frequent bitstring is checked against the clauses. For a unique solution, success probability equals the squared overlap with the ground state.
equations.justification: Follows from the diagonal H_P with a zero-energy ground space; the abstract says only that the final Hamiltonian state encodes the solution.

registers.name: data
registers.role: EC3 variable qubits; qubit i corresponds to counts string bits[::-1][i]

registers.name: anc
registers.role: optional ancilla for phase-kick filter, returned to |0>, not measured

specification.initial_state: |+>^{\otimes 3} on data (ground state of H_B), ancilla |0>

steps.description: Apply H to each data qubit to prepare the ground state of H_B.
Choose the EC3 clauses and expand H_P into Z, ZZ terms; compute the schedule s_k classically from the gap rule.
For k=1..M, apply the Trotter slice: RZ/CX-RZ-CX for H_P with angle proportional to s_k dt, then RX on every data qubit for H_B.
Optionally, every few steps apply the ancilla phase-kick filter and its inverse; skip it if it reduces to the identity.
Measure only the 3 data qubits in the computational basis, histogram, take the argmax, verify against the clauses.

specification.measurement: Measure the 3 data qubits in the computational basis; do not measure the ancilla. Counts key bits[::-1][i] gives data qubit i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Histogram counts, take the most frequent bitstring, reverse it to map to variable order, and verify that every clause has exactly one 1.
assumptions: Instance: 3 variables with a few clauses and a unique satisfying assignment, chosen by us
Noiseless simulation, so decoherence robustness is not tested
Phase-kick filter built from standard gates; no black box
missing_information: The paper's fast-signal form (random or regular) and how it assists the evolution
The concrete EC3 instance and schedule used in the paper
